During their E3 presentation, the Microsoft rep did say, "All devs need to do is approve their game. No other work is necessary." We'll see how true that is in the coming months. I really think it will. It's a good retention move for them. Don't sell your games, they're worthless second hand any way, but trade in your machine and buy all our new stuff.

Seems less about opening up games we love and more about filling up the arcade with titles. Hopefully they get all the rockstar and bethesda games. That would be a game changer.

I think this idea is a great one. If their vision for a continually expanding list of titles comes true and if it is really as easy as they think for developers to approve their game for it this will be a massive PR bump for Microsoft. Not only that, but it may get the hesitant last-gen gamers to buy an Xbox One knowing that they won't have to switch back and forth to play games with friends that haven't upgraded. This rings true further for people that might need to sell their last-gen consoles to help fund the purchase of the new ones.

While I think this is a good thing and Microsoft is on the right track I still think this should be a feature implemented from the beginning. We should encourage them but not give them too much praise for something that other platforms already have and that they should have had from day one.

Since I started vaping I wanted in that cloud game. But, I have no interest for charging 5 batteries all the time and constantly dripping juice on my coil. So I got the iStick50 watt with the Atlantis v2. Its cloud city. Look up a review for the Atlantis V2 and you will be impressed. If you can put together a tiny stick vape pen, you can work the Atlantis. Kanger subtank, arctic, and many other subtanks are good too but the atlantis in my opinion is better for beginners.
Want on that cloud game but aren't a skilled vaper? Read my recommendation.
There have been some problems with the iStick 50W so I can't really reccomend it anymore. But really any around 50 watt mod + any of the various good subohm tanks should have you "Clouding it up".
What problems with the istick 50w have you heard of? Mine works beautifully

Auto-firing issues and not firing issues. From what I can tell, people over drip or otherwise get juice into the device. This causes issues. I've since been recommending people place their faulty devices in bags of rice to dry them out and it has worked every time so far. Also a wipe down with iso alcohol helps while you're inside the device. I work at a shop and had to deal with an ungodly amount of returns before the problem was diagnosed.

Here's another example of the theory

I've never had it auto fire, but I'm on a subtank. I've had a few issues where it would stop firing in mid toke but its only when its really hot, or low on battery. The juice on the device isn't an issue with me.. and that bags of rice trick is universal to any water or liquid damaged electronic. I don't work at a shop anymore, but when I did the iStick30w sold like crazy, and I never had a return. I left before the 50w were in stock.

Yeah never had any 30 issues at our shop either.

I feel like the rice trick is common knowledge, but I don't think people realized that juice was the culprit so it's hard to diagnose a solution when you haven't identified the problem.

I'm glad your 50 watt is fine and you know how to not get juice everywhere! Happy vaping!
